research_rationale:
Read the whole order (53 FR 15649, signed 1988-04-28; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12638.txt): a recital that the Senate gave advice and consent to the Inter-American Convention on Letters Rogatory and Additional Protocol on October 9, 1986, that the President signed the instrument of ratification on November 10, 1986, and that the Convention requires contracting states to designate central authorities; section 1 designates the Department of Justice as the United States Central Authority to transmit and process letters rogatory and otherwise proceed in conformity with the Convention and Additional Protocol; section 2 authorizes the Department of Justice to make the additional designations the Convention and Additional Protocol provide for. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc has 0 hits, current-law:ecfr has 0 hits and later-events:ofr_catalog has 0 hits, so no U.S. Code note, regulation or Office of the Federal Register disposition note records an amendment, revocation or supersession. The only held text naming the order's number is its own printing. The authority the order cites, 3 U.S.C. 301, is held in the U.S. Code release point 119-121 text (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) and still authorizes the President to designate and empower the head of a department or agency to perform functions vested in the President, so the authority has not lapsed. Limitation disclosed: the packet holds no text of the Convention or of any denunciation of it, so continuation rests on the held original, the still-operative statute and the three bounded searches finding no later instrument.
